basic_information.name: Docling
basic_information.creator: IBM Research Zurich, AI for Knowledge team. Open-sourced in July 2024. Now hosted as a project in the LF AI & Data Foundation. Red Hat is a key integration partner (including Docling in RHEL AI). ~176 contributors on GitHub as of February 2026.
basic_information.description: Docling is an open-source, MIT-licensed Python library for converting documents (PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, HTML, images, audio) into structured, AI-ready formats (Markdown, HTML, DocTags, JSON). It uses state-of-the-art specialized AI models for layout analysis (DocLayNet, based on RT-DETR) and table structure recognition (TableFormer), plus the optional Granite-Docling-258M vision-language model for end-to-end document understanding. Docling runs entirely locally on commodity hardware, ensuring data privacy with no cloud dependencies. It is purpose-built for the RAG pipeline: its HybridChunker and HierarchicalChunker produce semantically coherent, metadata-rich chunks optimized for vector embedding. With 52.5K GitHub stars and plug-and-play integrations with LangChain, LlamaIndex, Haystack, and CrewAI, Docling has become the de facto open-source document ingestion layer for generative AI applications. It was the #1 trending repository on GitHub worldwide in November 2024.
basic_information.release_date: Open-sourced July 2024; latest version v2.72.0 released February 3, 2026 (150 total releases). Granite-Docling-258M model released September 2025. AAAI 2025 paper (arXiv:2501.17887). Original technical report arXiv:2408.09869 (August 2024).
basic_information.license: MIT License (Docling codebase and docling-mcp). Granite-Docling-258M model is Apache 2.0.

technical_architecture.architecture_type: Self-contained Python library with modular pipeline architecture. The core conversion pipeline chains: (1) document format parsers (PDF, DOCX, PPTX, etc.), (2) layout analysis model (DocLayNet/RT-DETR or Heron for faster parsing), (3) table structure recognition (TableFormer), (4) OCR engine (optional, for scanned content), and (5) output serializers (Markdown, HTML, DocTags, JSON). Can also run as an API server via docling-serve (FastAPI-based, with Docker/Kubernetes support and a dedicated Kubernetes Operator). The optional Granite-Docling-258M VLM consolidates multiple single-purpose models into one compact vision-language model built on Idefics3 architecture.
technical_architecture.language: Python (98.9% of codebase). Uses uv for package management, Ruff for linting, Pydantic v2 for data validation. Requires Python 3.10+ (3.9 support dropped in v2.70.0). C++ components in docling-parse for low-level PDF text extraction with coordinates.
technical_architecture.embedding_dimensions: Not directly applicable — Docling is a document processing/conversion tool, not an embedding model. However, it produces structured output (Markdown, JSON, DocTags) optimized for any downstream embedding model. The HybridChunker is tokenization-aware and can be configured for any embedding model's token limits.
technical_architecture.indexing_algorithm: Not applicable — Docling does not perform vector indexing. It sits upstream in the RAG pipeline, converting raw documents into structured representations suitable for chunking, embedding, and indexing by vector databases.
technical_architecture.scalability: Single-machine processing with linear scaling characteristics (benchmarked at 1.26 seconds/page across 4,000 pages). GPU acceleration supported (NVIDIA L4: 57-114ms/page median). docling-serve enables horizontal scaling via Kubernetes with the Docling Operator for distributed conversion jobs. Multiple container images available: CPU-only, CUDA 12.6, CUDA 12.8, AMD ROCm 6.3. Batch processing mode available for multi-document workloads.
technical_architecture.deployment_options: Python library (pip install docling), CLI tool, API server (docling-serve via Docker/Podman at quay.io/docling-project/docling-serve), Kubernetes deployment with Docling Operator, Docker Compose. Fully local execution — no cloud dependency. Available on IBM watsonx.ai. Red Hat RHEL AI integration planned. MCP server via docling-mcp for agentic AI integration.

rag_specific_capabilities.retrieval_method: Not directly applicable — Docling is a document processing layer, not a retrieval engine. However, it produces output specifically optimized for downstream retrieval systems. Its structured DoclingDocument representation preserves reading order, table structure, and hierarchical sections, enabling higher-quality dense vector and hybrid retrieval when passed to vector databases through frameworks like LangChain or LlamaIndex.
rag_specific_capabilities.chunking_strategy_support: Built-in document-structure-aware chunking via two strategies: (1) HierarchicalChunker — splits content into semantically coherent segments (sections, paragraphs, tables, figures) while preserving logical document hierarchy in metadata; (2) HybridChunker — two-pass strategy applying tokenization-aware refinements on top of hierarchical chunking, with intelligent splitting of oversized chunks and merging of undersized chunks with matching context. Both chunkers leverage the rich structural metadata from Docling's conversion pipeline, producing chunks with section headings, page numbers, and element types as metadata.
rag_specific_capabilities.reranking_support: Not built-in — Docling focuses on document conversion and chunking. Reranking is handled by downstream frameworks (LangChain, LlamaIndex, Haystack) that consume Docling's output.
rag_specific_capabilities.multimodal_support: Strong multimodal document processing: extracts and classifies images, charts, tables, code blocks, mathematical equations (LaTeX), and figures from documents. Granite-Docling-258M provides vision-language understanding for charts (converting to table format), formulas (to LaTeX), code blocks (to text), and layout analysis. Supports image input formats (PNG, TIFF, JPEG). Audio support via Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) models for WAV, MP3, VTT formats. Image extraction and embedded image handling available in docling-serve.
rag_specific_capabilities.graph_rag_support: No built-in knowledge graph construction. Docling produces structured document representations that preserve hierarchical relationships (sections, subsections, references) which could feed into graph construction pipelines, but this is left to downstream tools.
rag_specific_capabilities.citation_grounding: Docling preserves source attribution metadata throughout the conversion pipeline. Each chunk produced by the chunkers includes provenance information (source document, page number, section heading, element type). This metadata enables downstream RAG systems to provide accurate source citations. The DocTags format explicitly captures element locations and contextual relationships within documents.
rag_specific_capabilities.context_window_optimization: The HybridChunker is tokenization-aware: it can be configured with specific tokenizer models to produce chunks that respect token limits. Intelligent splitting/merging ensures chunks are neither too large (exceeding context windows) nor too small (losing semantic coherence). The hierarchical metadata enables downstream systems to implement context compression or selective retrieval strategies.

performance_and_benchmarks.latency: Per-page processing latency varies by hardware: x86 CPU median 0.79s/page (p5: 0.6s, p95: 16.3s); Apple M3 Max median 0.32s/page (p5: 0.26s, p95: 6.48s); NVIDIA L4 GPU median 0.114s/page (p5: 57ms, p95: 2.08s). Aggregate benchmark: 1.26s/page across 89 PDFs and 4,000 pages. Single-page processing: ~6.28s; 50-page document: ~65.12s with linear scaling.
performance_and_benchmarks.throughput: Linear scaling with document size (predictable performance for enterprise workloads). Processing 4,000 pages across 89 PDFs at 1.26s/page. GPU-accelerated mode (NVIDIA L4) can process ~8-9 pages/second. docling-serve enables concurrent processing for higher throughput via API server mode.
performance_and_benchmarks.accuracy_metrics: Granite-Docling-258M benchmarks: Table recognition TEDS-structure 0.97, TEDS with content 0.96 (FinTabNet @150dpi). Full-page OCR F1 0.84, edit-distance 0.45. Code recognition F1 0.988, edit-distance 0.013. Equation recognition F1 0.968, edit-distance 0.073. Layout detection MAP 0.27, F1 0.86. OCRBench score 500. MMStar 0.30. Overall 97.9% accuracy on complex table extraction from sustainability report benchmarks.
performance_and_benchmarks.benchmark_results: In Procycons PDF Data Extraction Benchmark 2025 (comparing Docling, Unstructured, LlamaParse): Docling achieved superior accuracy (97.9% complex table extraction) with predictable linear scaling. Outperformed Unstructured (75% on complex tables, highly inconsistent speed) and competitive with LlamaParse (faster constant-time but lower accuracy on complex structures). Docling outperformed Marker and MinerU in speed tests. Granite-Docling-258M significantly outperforms SmolDocling-256M across all metrics (e.g., table TEDS 0.97 vs 0.82, OCRBench 500 vs 338).

integration_and_ecosystem.framework_compatibility: First-class plug-and-play integrations with: LangChain (DoclingLoader document loader, documented at docs.langchain.com), LlamaIndex (DoclingReader with RAG examples), Haystack (integration for pipeline-based document processing), CrewAI (for agentic AI workflows), spaCy (NLP pipeline integration). Official RAG tutorial examples for both LangChain and LlamaIndex in the Docling documentation. Also integrated with Pathway for real-time multimodal data processing and OpenSearch for vector search pipelines.
integration_and_ecosystem.model_compatibility: Model-agnostic output — Docling converts documents to standard formats (Markdown, JSON, HTML) consumable by any LLM. Built-in models: DocLayNet (layout analysis, RT-DETR based), TableFormer (table structure), Heron (faster layout model), Granite-Docling-258M (end-to-end VLM, Apache 2.0). The VLM uses siglip2-base-patch16-512 vision encoder + Granite 165M LLM. Compatible with any downstream LLM: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Mistral, IBM Granite, open-source models via the consuming RAG framework.
integration_and_ecosystem.mcp_integration_status: Yes — official docling-mcp package (MIT license, v1.3.2) provides a Model Context Protocol server. Capabilities: document-to-markdown conversion (URL or local path), image extraction, table extraction as structured data, batch document processing, Q&A document generation (YAML format). Installable via uvx and configurable in Claude Desktop, Cursor, and other MCP-compatible clients.
integration_and_ecosystem.data_source_connectors: Docling processes documents from: local filesystem paths, URLs (HTTP/HTTPS), and programmatic input via Python API. Supported input formats: PDF (programmatic and scanned), DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, HTML, AsciiDoc, images (PNG, TIFF, JPEG), audio (WAV, MP3, VTT). No built-in connectors for cloud storage (S3, GCS) or collaboration tools (Confluence, Notion, Slack) — these are handled by the consuming framework (LangChain, LlamaIndex) or custom pipeline code.
integration_and_ecosystem.observability_integration: No built-in observability or tracing. Docling is a library/CLI tool focused on document conversion. Observability for the full RAG pipeline is handled by the consuming framework (LangSmith with LangChain, Langfuse with LlamaIndex, etc.). docling-serve API server provides standard HTTP logging and health endpoints.

pricing_and_cost.pricing_model: Fully free and open-source (MIT license). No paid tiers, no per-document fees, no API usage charges. Self-hosted only — no managed cloud service from IBM specifically for Docling. Available within IBM watsonx.ai platform (IBM's commercial pricing applies there). Granite-Docling-258M model is free (Apache 2.0) with 215K+ monthly downloads on Hugging Face.
pricing_and_cost.free_tier: Everything is free. MIT-licensed library with no usage limits. All models (DocLayNet, TableFormer, Heron, Granite-Docling-258M) are freely available. No cloud-hosted service with tiered pricing exists.
pricing_and_cost.cost_at_scale: Infrastructure costs only: CPU-based processing at ~1.26s/page means a single machine can process ~2,800 pages/hour. GPU-accelerated (NVIDIA L4) can process ~8-9 pages/second (~32,000 pages/hour). No per-document or per-page software fees. Cloud GPU costs apply if using GPU acceleration (e.g., AWS g6.xlarge ~$0.80/hour for L4 GPU). For 1M pages: ~357 CPU-hours ($35-70 on cloud VMs) or ~31 GPU-hours ($25-50 on cloud GPUs).
pricing_and_cost.total_cost_of_ownership: Software licensing: $0. Compute costs: $30-200/month for moderate workloads on a cloud VM (CPU-only). GPU costs additional if needed for throughput ($0.50-1.00/hour per L4 GPU). Storage: minimal (Docling processes documents but doesn't store them). No embedding costs (handled separately by embedding model choice). No vendor lock-in risks. Ops overhead: low for library usage, moderate for docling-serve API deployment, higher for Kubernetes Operator deployment. Total for a startup processing 100K pages/month: ~$50-150/month infrastructure.

adoption_and_market.market_position: Leader in open-source document conversion for AI/RAG pipelines. #1 trending GitHub repository worldwide in November 2024. Fastest-growing open-source document processing tool in 2024-2025. Positioned as the de facto document ingestion layer for the open-source generative AI ecosystem. Backed by IBM Research with LF AI & Data Foundation governance. Competitive with commercial solutions (LlamaParse, Reducto) while being fully free and locally executable.
adoption_and_market.notable_customers: Red Hat (integrating Docling into RHEL AI for enterprise customers to ingest private data for InstructLab synthetic data generation). IBM watsonx.ai (internal adoption). LF AI & Data Foundation project. Used broadly in enterprise document AI pipelines, sustainability reporting analysis, financial document processing, and research paper conversion. Specific named enterprise customers not publicly disclosed, but 52.5K GitHub stars and 215K+ monthly model downloads indicate widespread adoption across industries. [uncertain]
adoption_and_market.community_size: 52.5K GitHub stars (February 2026), 176 contributors, 150 releases. Granite-Docling-258M: 215,340 monthly downloads on Hugging Face. Part of the docling-project GitHub organization (multiple repos: docling, docling-core, docling-parse, docling-ibm-models, docling-serve, docling-mcp, docling-operator). Active GitHub Discussions for community support. Hosted in LF AI & Data Foundation.
adoption_and_market.funding_and_valuation: Not applicable as a standalone product — Docling is an open-source project from IBM Research (IBM market cap ~$230B). IBM invested in the project through its Research division in Zurich. The project's governance was transferred to the LF AI & Data Foundation for community-driven development. No separate funding or valuation for Docling as an entity.
adoption_and_market.competitive_landscape: Main competitors: (1) LlamaParse (LlamaIndex) — cloud-based, fast constant-time processing (~6s any size), freemium model, but less accurate on complex tables and requires API dependency; (2) Unstructured — open-core, strong OCR, but significantly slower (51s for 1 page) and inconsistent scaling; (3) Marker — lightweight open-source PDF-to-Markdown, fast but less feature-rich; (4) MinerU — open-source alternative, slower than Docling; (5) Reducto — commercial document parser; (6) LLMWhisperer (Unstract) — commercial alternative. Docling differentiators: (a) fully local/private execution, (b) MIT license with no cloud dependency, (c) best-in-class table extraction accuracy (97.9%), (d) Granite-Docling-258M compact VLM, (e) LF AI Foundation governance, (f) broadest format support (PDF+DOCX+PPTX+XLSX+HTML+images+audio).

entrepreneurial_relevance.startup_applicability: Best for: any startup building RAG applications that need to ingest diverse document formats (contracts, reports, presentations, spreadsheets). Team size: works for solo developers up to large engineering teams. Budget: $0 software cost — only infrastructure needed. Use case fit: document Q&A chatbots, knowledge bases from enterprise documents, compliance document processing, financial report analysis, legal document ingestion, research paper processing. Particularly strong for: (a) startups handling sensitive/regulated documents (fully local, no data leaves the machine), (b) teams that need table-heavy document processing (97.9% accuracy), (c) European/GDPR-conscious startups (no cloud dependency, data stays on-premise). Not recommended for: teams that only need simple text extraction from clean PDFs (overkill — use PyMuPDF), or teams needing real-time streaming document processing (Docling is batch-oriented).
entrepreneurial_relevance.build_vs_buy_guidance: Use Docling library directly when: building a custom RAG pipeline, need maximum control over document processing, data privacy is paramount, budget is constrained. Use docling-serve when: need a shared document processing API for multiple applications, want Docker/Kubernetes deployment, need to scale processing across a team. Use LlamaParse instead when: need fastest time-to-result with zero infrastructure, acceptable to send documents to a cloud API, primarily working with PDFs only. Use Unstructured instead when: need broader ETL pipeline features beyond document conversion, willing to pay for managed service. Self-hosting Docling is straightforward (pip install or Docker), making it the default choice for most startups that value data privacy and cost control.
entrepreneurial_relevance.time_to_production: POC: 30 minutes to 2 hours (pip install docling, convert first document, inspect output). MVP with RAG: 1-3 days (integrate with LangChain/LlamaIndex, configure chunking strategy, connect to vector database, build simple Q&A). Production deployment: 1-2 weeks (optimize chunking parameters, set up docling-serve API, configure GPU acceleration if needed, integrate monitoring). Kubernetes deployment with Docling Operator: 2-4 weeks (includes infrastructure setup, scaling configuration, CI/CD pipeline).
key_lessons: 1. Document processing quality is the #1 determinant of RAG accuracy — Garbage in, garbage out applies doubly to RAG. Docling's 97.9% table extraction accuracy directly translates to better retrieval results. Invest time in document conversion quality before tuning embeddings or prompts. A startup that processes documents well with Docling will outperform competitors using fast-but-sloppy parsers.

2. Local-first document processing eliminates your biggest enterprise sales objection — When selling AI products to regulated industries (finance, healthcare, legal), the question 'where does our data go?' kills deals. Docling runs 100% locally with no cloud dependency, so you can truthfully say 'your documents never leave your infrastructure.' This is a competitive moat against cloud-only alternatives like LlamaParse.

3. Start with HybridChunker, not fixed-size chunks — Most RAG tutorials use naive fixed-size chunking, which destroys table structure and section context. Docling's HybridChunker preserves document hierarchy while respecting token limits. The 30 minutes spent configuring it properly saves weeks of debugging poor retrieval quality later.

4. The Granite-Docling-258M model is your secret weapon for complex documents — At only 258M parameters, it runs on commodity hardware while matching models 10x its size on table recognition (TEDS 0.97). Use it for documents with complex layouts, charts, equations, and code blocks. Skip it for simple text-heavy documents where the default pipeline is faster.

5. Use docling-mcp to make document processing agentic — The MCP server integration means AI agents (Claude, custom agents) can autonomously convert and query documents. This enables building self-service document intelligence products where users drop in files and get answers, without building custom document processing UIs.
entrepreneurial_relevance.no_code_interface: docling-serve provides a web UI at http://localhost:5001/ui for document conversion without code. The MCP server (docling-mcp) enables document processing through AI assistants like Claude Desktop without writing code. No dedicated visual/drag-and-drop pipeline builder — for visual RAG pipeline building, combine Docling with Dify or RAGFlow.
entrepreneurial_relevance.session_mapping: Session 3 (Framing & managing AI projects — Build vs Buy decisions for document processing in RAG pipelines), Session 4 (AI business models — cost analysis of self-hosted vs cloud document processing, unit economics of document AI)

confidence.data_quality: High — information sourced from official GitHub repository (52.5K stars), IBM Research blog, Hugging Face model card, arXiv papers (2408.09869, 2501.17887), PyPI, and third-party benchmarks (Procycons 2025). IBM Research is a highly credible source. Project is well-documented with active development (150 releases, v2.72.0 as of February 2026).
confidence.cross_reference: GitHub repository data confirmed across PyPI, Hugging Face, and IBM Research blog. Benchmark numbers cross-referenced between arXiv papers and third-party evaluations (Procycons benchmark). Granite-Docling-258M performance confirmed on Hugging Face model card and InfoQ/MarkTechPost coverage. LF AI Foundation hosting confirmed by multiple sources. Red Hat RHEL AI integration confirmed by Red Hat official blog.
confidence.caveats: GitHub stars (52.5K) include significant growth from viral trending in November 2024 — actual active production usage may be lower than stars suggest. Processing speed benchmarks vary significantly by document complexity (p5 vs p95 range is 10-30x). The Granite-Docling-258M model's multilingual support (Japanese, Arabic, Chinese) is marked experimental. Docling's architecture description claiming it is 'built upon the Unstructured framework' from one source appears to be an error in that source — Docling is an independent project. Audio processing support (WAV/MP3) is a newer feature and may be less battle-tested than PDF processing. Some benchmark comparisons may not be fully apples-to-apples across different evaluation setups.
confidence.security_posture: Strong privacy-by-design: fully local execution with no data sent to external APIs. No known embedding inversion or knowledge base poisoning vectors specific to Docling (these are downstream concerns for the RAG system, not the document converter). MIT license allows full audit of source code. LF AI & Data Foundation governance provides institutional oversight. docling-serve supports TLS encryption between components on Kubernetes. For enterprise deployments, Red Hat RHEL AI integration provides additional security hardening. No documented CVEs specific to Docling as of February 2026. Potential attack surface: maliciously crafted PDFs could theoretically exploit the PDF parser — standard PDF security considerations apply.
